cues.en: So what's the idea
behind ChatGPT's Code Interpreter feature?
Well, one very important use case for using ChatGPT,
which we'll also explore in this course
is to use ChatGPT to generate code.
Because ChatGPT is capable of generating code
for a vast variety of programming languages.
But without Code Interpreter,
you then have to take that generated code
and execute it on your own, which often also means
that you need to install or set up extra tools
that might be required to execute that code.
With Code Interpreter, ChatGPT is not just able
to generate the code,
but it's also able to execute that code.
It's able to execute those generated code snippets
in an isolated restricted execution environment.
And therefore, certain restrictions
to which I will come back will apply.
And at this point of time, it's also just Python code
that can be executed.
Nonetheless, this is, of course, an extremely useful feature
that can be used for a broad variety of use cases.
You could use this feature to perform
mathematical calculations and you would no longer face
the danger of running into hallucinations,
since with Code Interpreter, ChatGPT is now able
to simply write the code that will then perform
the mathematical calculation
instead of trying to predict the result,
which can sometimes be wrong.
You could also use Code Interpreter to generate dummy data,
or extract information from files,
or transform file content.
You can use it for data science to load and clean data
and, of course, to analyze data and build charts.
And you can also use it for image editing,
for example, to analyze and transform images,
or do other exciting things with images.
And there might be more use cases,
where you want to use Code Interpreter,
because even though these here are probably
the most important and common use cases,
as with ChatGPT in general,
it's, of course, ultimately your imagination
that's the limit.
Though speaking of limits,
Code Interpreter definitely has some limits,
because the code that gets generated and executed by ChatGPT
is executed in an isolated execution environment
provided by OpenAI.
So that code that's generated and executed
is executed on machines owned and operated by OpenAI.
And therefore, certain restrictions set by OpenAI do apply.
For example, at the moment,
OpenAI only provides an execution environment
for Python code.
So you can't execute other code with Code Interpreter
at this point of time,
though that, of course, may change over time.
In addition, the code that is being executed
in that environment does not have internet access.
So if you are trying to run some code,
that would need to reach out to the internet,
for example, to crawl and summarize a website,
that code would fail and would not work.
In addition, this environment, of course, also has no access
to your local hard drive, because as I just mentioned,
that code's running on some machine owned
and operated by OpenAI.
It's not running on your system
and it therefore doesn't have access to your system,
which, of course, in general is a good thing.
But if you are trying to run some code that needs to work
with data that's stored on your machine,
that code also would fail,
though ChatGPT actually does allow you
to also upload and download files.
when using Code Interpreter.
Though, of course, you should definitely take a look
at OpenAI's privacy policy to understand
how they might be using or storing the data
you are sharing with them,
for example, through file uploads.
Because you might not want to share
super sensitive internal company data, for example.
At least, you should be aware of how OpenAI
is going to use that data.
Now, in addition, in that execution environment,
there is only a selected list
of extra code packages available.
And with that, I mean extra packages
that contain some extra code that could be used
to execute your code.
For example, there are packages that help
with image manipulation or with QR code generation.
And whilst this environment that's provided by OpenAI
comes with many pre-installed utility packages
that might be needed to run the code
you need to run for a given task,
there also might be certain tasks you might want to perform
with help of Code Interpreter,
that just won't work, because a certain package
that might be needed might be missing.
Though in our experience, Code Interpreter and ChatGPT
are doing quite well when it comes to identifying
such situations and are then often able to generate
and execute some alternative code that does not require
a certain package that might be missing.
Last but not least,
another important Code Interpreter restriction
is that it's only available for ChatGPT Plus users
and not in the free version.
